q.t: 8 hundreds, 3 tens and 2 ones make which number?
q.e: Write the hundreds, tens and ones digits in order: 8, 3, 2.

q.t: 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones make which number?
q.e: There are no tens, so 0 holds the tens place: 5 0 4.

q.t: 7 hundreds and nothing else make which number?
q.e: No tens and no ones, so both of those places get a 0.

q.t: What is one more than 999?
q.e: Ones, tens and hundreds are all full, so they roll over to one thousand.
3 hundreds, 6 tens and 8 ones: 368.

q.t: Between which two hundreds does 468 lie?
q.e: 468 has 4 hundreds, so it is after 400 and before 500.

q.t: Birbal said there were 963 crows. Which is its number name?
q.e: 9 hundreds, 6 tens (sixty) and 3 ones (three).
Adding 10 adds one ten: 5 tens become 6 tens.

q.t: How many hundreds make 1000?
q.e: Counting in hundreds: 100, 200 … 1000 is ten hundreds.

q.t: Between which two tens does 468 lie?
q.e: 468 has 46 tens and 8 ones, so it is after 460 and before 470.

q.t: Between which two fifties does 468 lie?
q.e: Fifties go 400, 450, 500 … and 468 is after 450 but before 500.

q.t: A crane is at 667 and wants to reach 700. How many steps forward?
A crane is at 667 and wants to reach 650. How many steps back?
Adding 25 each time: 850, 875, 900, ___. What comes next?
Adding 100 each time: 330, 430, 530, ___. What comes next?
q.e: Adding 100 changes only the hundreds digit: 5 becomes 6.

q.t: Which number reads the same from left to right and from right to left?
q.e: 353 backwards is still 3-5-3. The others change when reversed.

q.t: What is two more than 610?
What is the greatest 3-digit number?
q.e: Each place can hold at most 9, so 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 9 ones. One more would be 1000, a 4-digit number.

q.t: You have 6 paper slips. On each you can write 100, 10 or 1. What is the largest number the 6 slips can make?
q.e: Write 100 on every slip: 6 hundreds = 600.

q.t: Using the same 6 slips (each 100, 10 or 1), what is the smallest number you can make?
q.e: Write 1 on every slip: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.

q.t: To make 231 with slips of 100, 10 and 1, how many slips do you need?
q.e: 2 slips of 100, 3 slips of 10 and 1 slip of 1: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6.

q.t: Which number can NOT be made with exactly 6 slips (each 100, 10 or 1)?
q.e: 999 needs 9 + 9 + 9 = 27 slips. 123 needs 1 + 2 + 3 = 6, 600 needs 6, and 42 needs 4 + 2 = 6.

q.t: Using only the digits 3 and 8 (you may repeat them), what is the largest 3-digit number?
q.e: Use the bigger digit, 8, in every place.

q.t: Make the smallest 3-digit number using the digits 3 and 8, using each at least once.
q.e: Put 3 in the hundreds and tens places to keep it small, then 8 must go in the ones place.

q.t: In word numerals, ‘moon’ means 1 (there is one moon) and ‘eyes’ means 2. What number is ‘eyes moon’, read left to right?
q.e: Each word stands for one digit: eyes = 2 then moon = 1, so 2 1 = 21.

q.t: What is a century plus a half century?
q.e: A century is 100 and a half century is half of 100, which is 50: 150.

q.t: Riddle: I am between 400 and 450. My tens digit is 3 and my ones digit is 5. Who am I?
q.e: Between 400 and 450 means 4 hundreds; then 3 tens and 5 ones: 435.

q.t: There were 963 crows. 48 flew away and then 25 more came. How many crows now?
Counting on by 15: 905, 920, 935, ___. What comes next?
Put 384, 23, 176 and 905 in order from smallest to largest. Which number is second?
q.e: 23 has no hundreds, then 176 (1 hundred), 384 (3), 905 (9). The second is 176.

q.t: A driver shows his rice sacks with 9 hundred tiles, 4 ten tiles and 7 one tiles. He unloads 2 hundred sacks. How many sacks are left?
q.e: He had 947. Taking away 200 changes only the hundreds digit: 9 becomes 7.

q.t: Riddle: I am between 570 and 630. My tens digit is 1 and my ones digit is 5. Who am I?
q.e: Between 570 and 630 with tens digit 1 can only be in the 600s: 615.

q.t: Which number lies between 595 and 605?
q.e: 599 is more than 595 and less than 605. The others are outside.

q.t: Between which two hundreds does 750 lie?
q.e: 750 has 7 hundreds, so it comes after 700 and before 800 — exactly in the middle.

q.t: How many tens make 1000?
q.e: 100 has 10 tens, and 1000 is ten hundreds: 10 × 10 = 100 tens.

q.t: How many 3-digit numbers between 200 and 300 read the same from both ends?
q.e: They must start and end with 2: 202, 212, 222 … 292 — one for each middle digit 0 to 9.

q.t: Rita has 3 notes of ₹100, 6 notes of ₹10 and 8 coins of ₹1. She needs ₹400. How much more does she need?
